title: Uxmal
summary: Uxmal is a Maya town of the Puuc region in Yucatan, founded around 700 CE and home to some 25,000 people, with buildings dating from 700 to 1000. ICOMOS records that it was abandoned around 1200. The Pyramid of the Soothsayer, also called the Pyramid of the Magician, dominates the ceremonial centre; it is 35 m high and elliptical in plan, made of five superimposed elements.

uncertainty.note: Start is 'founded c. A.D. 700' (UNESCO); buildings date 700-1000 (UNESCO) and the town was 'abandoned around 1200' (ICOMOS evaluation).

phases.description: The pyramid is of the Late Classic Period (AD 700-900); the final phase, Temple V, was built around 1000-1050.
No further building phase is recorded after Temple V; the town was abandoned around 1200.
Uxmal was abandoned around 1200 according to the ICOMOS evaluation and the Spanish later renamed its buildings.

reviewer_note: Pyramid modelled as stepped_pyramid although the plan is elliptical; the 35 m height and 85 x 50 m ellipse are from the 1996 ICOMOS evaluation (the PDF's text layer garbles the plan, I read '85 m x 50 m' from the page image). Popular accounts (not opened) give a smaller base; the ICOMOS value is the only one cited. The 'ruined' phase from 1200 is a loose reading: ICOMOS says the town was abandoned around 1200 but also that inhabitants returned and it was a pilgrimage place until the Spanish. Materials: WHE says the buildings of Uxmal are limestone.
